correction_note.what_was_wrong: cipher/rubato.go's Gaussian noise sampler (noiseAGN) drew from a Box-Muller transform over crypto/rand-sourced uniform floats -- an approximate Gaussian, not the reference's actual discrete Gaussian sampler (ckks_fv/RtF_bench_test.go:659's ring.GaussianSampler, ldsec/lattigo's ring package). This was never verified statistically equivalent to the reference. Rubato's security rests on an LWE-style assumption stated over Gaussian error, so an unverified substitute distribution is a correctness bug, not a performance detail -- caught by review, not by either correctness gate (Gate A compares at sigma=0; Gate B only checks that CKKS's tolerance absorbs the residual error's magnitude, which a wrong-but-similarly-small distribution would also pass).
correction_note.fix: noiseAGN now calls ldsec/lattigo's ring.GaussianSampler.AGN directly (cipher/rubato.go), via a go.mod `replace` pointing at the pinned third_party/RtF-Transciphering checkout (AGN is a KAIST-CryptLab addition, not present in the public github.com/ldsec/lattigo/v2 module, confirmed by fetching and diffing both). Sampler is now allocated once (sync.Once) and reused across calls, not reconstructed per Encrypt(). Added TestRubatoNoiseStatistics (cipher/rubato_test.go): empirical mean and std dev of 30,000 noise draws vs. RubatoSigma, PASS (mean=-0.019, stddev 1.4-1.5% off sigma across runs).
correction_note.consequence_for_prior_numbers: The prior artifact's per-element ratios (Rubato ~3.05x HERA with noise, ~1.19x without) were measured against the wrong sampler and do NOT survive as a Rubato property -- the wrong sampler's overhead (711 allocs/op, largely crypto/rand.Int calls) was the dominant cost, not Rubato's algebra. With the correct, reference sampler (199 allocs/op), the finding REVERSES: Rubato is now measured CHEAPER than HERA, both per-record and per-element. See axis_b below for corrected numbers. The prior per-record ratios (~1.75-2.25x) were smaller in magnitude than the per-element ones but were still measured with the same wrong sampler feeding into Encrypt(), so they are superseded too, not just the per-element figures.
correction_note.not_affected_by_this_bug: Gate B's Rubato harness (toy_correctness/testdata/ckks_fv_patch/rtf_toy_correctness_rubato128l_test.go) calls ckks_fv's own plainRubato directly, which already used the real ring.GaussianSampler -- it was never affected by this bug. Only the client Go module (cipher/rubato.go) and everything measured from it (axis_b, both prior and corrected) were affected. Empirically re-confirmed this pass -- see gate_b_resource_usage's reverification.
correction_note.build_prerequisite_introduced: Fixing this the correct way (calling the reference sampler, not a local re-implementation) means tools/transciphering now requires third_party/ to be vendored (third_party/fetch_rtf.sh) BEFORE `go build ./...` -- go.mod replaces github.com/ldsec/lattigo/v2 with a relative path to third_party/RtF-Transciphering, since AGN is a KAIST-CryptLab addition absent from the public lattigo/v2 module (confirmed by fetching v2.4.1 from the public proxy and diffing). Previously only toy_correctness/'s staged tests needed third_party/ present; now the whole module does. Checked: doesn't break Docker or CI -- neither Dockerfile invokes the Go toolchain and no CI workflow exists in this repo. See tools/transciphering/README.md's Build/run section.

per_element_normalization.description: HERA-16 yields HeraStateSize=16 usable keystream elements per block; Rubato-128L yields RubatoOutputSize=60. Isolated via cipher/block_bench_test.go (BenchmarkHERABlock, BenchmarkRubatoBlock, BenchmarkRubatoBlockNoNoise -- now a permanent, committed benchmark, not a throwaway file), go test ./cipher/... -bench . -benchtime=100000x -count=7 -run '^$', all three run together in ONE invocation for a genuine same-session comparison. Machine state: powersave governor, AC power, load average 1.19-1.53 (low/clean), 2026-08-18T11:28:27Z-11:28:45Z. Values below are the median of 7 repetitions.
per_element_normalization.why_the_no_noise_figure_changed_from_248: Investigated explicitly, not assumed. encryptBlock's `if sigma > 0` guard means noiseAGN (and therefore the Gaussian sampler, old buggy or new correct) is NEVER called on the sigma=0 path -- confirmed by reading the current code, not inferred. The no-noise path is byte-identical code before and after the sampler fix. The prior 248.1 ns/element figure came from a SINGLE go test -bench invocation at -benchtime=2000x (2,000 iterations, no repetition) -- a low-power, unreliable methodology, not a real effect of the code change. The two more rigorous re-measurements since (a 5-repetition run at -benchtime=100000x during initial re-measurement, and this 7-repetition run) both converge to ~144-146 ns/element independently, in separate sessions -- that convergence, not the original 248.1 figure, is the trustworthy number. Conclusion: the original with-noise/without-noise comparison (3.05x vs 1.19x) OVERSTATED how much of Rubato's cost was noise-sampler-specific, because its without-noise baseline (248.1) was itself measured unreliably low-power and happened to run high, not because the sampler fix changed that code path -- treat the earlier 'noise added 158% overhead' framing as retired, not as a real pre/post-fix comparison.
per_element_normalization.headline: Per keystream element, Rubato-128L costs ~0.77x HERA WITH its Gaussian noise included (what Encrypt() actually does), and ~0.57x without it -- Rubato remains cheaper both ways, confirmed by a same-invocation, 7-repetition measurement under low, clean load. This refines (does not retract) the direction found in the first post-fix pass (~0.70x/~0.53x from a less rigorous 5-repetition run) -- the reversal from the original wrong-sampler numbers (3.05x/1.19x) is real and robust across multiple independent, methodologically-sound re-measurements. What changed between passes was measurement rigor for the WITHOUT-noise baseline specifically (see why_the_no_noise_figure_changed above), not the magnitude of the with/without-noise gap, which is now consistently ~35-40% (noise overhead) across the two rigorous passes -- a smaller gap than the original (unreliable) comparison implied. Plausible driver of Rubato being cheaper overall, not independently isolated this session: HERA needs HeraRounds+1=6 round-key rows (96 sampleZqx calls per 16-element block = 6/element) vs Rubato's RubatoRounds+1=3 rows (192 calls per 60-element block = 3.2/element) -- HERA does relatively more round-key-derivation work per unit of useful output. Hypothesis consistent with the result's direction, not independently confirmed by isolating sampleZqx cost.

multiplicative_depth_argument.description: The client-side numbers above measure PLAINTEXT arithmetic cost, which is not what determines homomorphic (server-side, FHE) evaluation cost. FHE cost is dominated by multiplicative depth -- the number of SEQUENTIALLY-DEPENDENT ciphertext-ciphertext multiplications (each needing relinearization and consuming noise budget), not by how many total arithmetic operations a plaintext CPU performs. See tools/transciphering/README.md's 'Multiplicative depth' section for the full argument; summary here. Unaffected by the noise-sampler bug/fix -- this section's content is unchanged from the prior artifact version.
multiplicative_depth_argument.hera_depth: 5 rounds x degree-3 cube S-box (x -> x^3 = x^2 . x). Each cube is 2 SEQUENTIAL ciphertext multiplications (fv_hera.go:355-363: x2=Mul(ct,ct); Relin; x3=Mul(x2,ct); Relin). 5 cube() calls total (4 in the round loop + 1 in finalization) x 2 mults each = 10 multiplicative levels.
multiplicative_depth_argument.rubato_128L_depth: 2 rounds x degree-2 Feistel-square (state[i] += state[i-1]^2). Each feistel() call squares blocksize-1=63 DIFFERENT, mutually-independent state elements (fv_rubato.go:734-741) -- these are logically PARALLEL, not sequentially dependent, so one feistel() call costs exactly 1 multiplicative level regardless of state size. 2 feistel() calls total (1 in the round loop + 1 in finalization) x 1 mult level each = 2 multiplicative levels.
multiplicative_depth_argument.implication: By this depth count, Rubato-128L's homomorphic evaluation should require ~5x fewer sequential ciphertext multiplications than HERA-16's -- the design rationale behind Rubato's noise mechanism (Ha et al., Eurocrypt 2022). Note this is now DIRECTIONALLY CONSISTENT with the corrected client-side numbers above (Rubato cheaper, not just closer) even though the client-side numbers still do not test multiplicative depth at all -- they measure a different thing (plaintext CPU cost) that happens to now point the same direction. That agreement should not be read as confirmation of the depth argument; it could as easily be coincidental given how different the two cost models are.
multiplicative_depth_argument.deciding_comparison_status: BLOCKED. The actual homomorphic-evaluation cost comparison (mfvHera.Crypt vs mfvRubato.Crypt wall time, at full or even toy scale with proper timing instrumentation) is the measurement that would confirm or refute this depth argument, and it has not been done at full scale (vendor_server's BFV eval is stub-only) or precisely at toy scale (gate_b_resource_usage above gives whole-test wall time/RSS for the full HalfBoot pipeline, not isolated Crypt()-call timing per cipher). This remains the single most important open measurement for this task.

Fixed by depending on the reference primitive directly. See correction_note above.

sourcing.rubato_variant_choice: Rubato-128L (RUBATO128L: n=64, r=2, q=0x1fc0001, sigma=1.6356633496458739795537788457309656607510203877762320964302959 -- fv_rubato.go:48-53). Grassi et al. (CRYPTO 2023, eprint 2023/822 Section 6.1/7.1, p.22, read directly this task) state the attack's bound 'cannot be established' for Rubato-128L specifically, unlike the other five variants. This means Rubato-128L is NOT COVERED by this attack's established bound -- not the same as proven secure. This benchmark is a performance/feasibility comparison, not a security endorsement.
sourcing.constants_not_fabricated: Every cipher constant, matrix coefficient, and derivation formula used in cipher/hera.go and cipher/rubato.go is cited in-code to an exact ckks_fv file/line at the pinned SHA 105fc73115b56f1d6ff357029c7682b19a6d8510, OR (for the Gaussian noise sampler, after this correction) calls that exact reference implementation directly rather than re-deriving it. The previous 'Table 3 of Cho et al. 2021' citation for heraRC was discarded, not re-sourced or replaced with another placeholder.
